data.narrative:
Calogena is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised €100M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a nuclear energy peer universe of 11 total comparables: 3 publicly traded firms (Oklo, Nano Nuclear Energy, and SMR) and 8 private companies including Fuse Energy, X-Energy, and General Matter.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable due to insufficient filtering depth. While 4 same-sector peers exist in nuclear energy, narrowing to peers at identical or adjacent stages with similar valuation tiers yielded fewer than 3 datapoints—the minimum threshold for reliable median-based triangulation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material sector heterogeneity bias given nuclear energy's distinct capex and regulatory profile relative to adjacent cleantech segments.

Without a sufficiently dense same-stage comparable set, the analysis cannot derive a defensible valuation range from traditional multiples-based methods. The 11-firm comp universe provides directional context for relative positioning within nuclear energy, but lacks the precision necessary for point or range estimation at Series A. Any valuation conclusion would require either: (1) relaxing stage/sector filters with explicit discount/premium justification, (2) alternative methods such as DCF or cost-of-capital approaches, or (3) accumulation of additional Series A nuclear peers. The current dataset supports comparative positioning only, not absolute pricing.
